universal_lens: The universal lens unifies discrete state transitions (faceoff wins/losses) with continuous expected value flows (expected goals, incremental zone time). It models the deterministic establishment of puck possession as a stochastic operator acting on spatial-temporal manifolds, mapping micro-mechanical advantages directly to macroscopic championship probabilities.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps faceoff outcomes into a Bayesian hierarchical framework, treating raw win percentages as latent priors. Conformal inference bounds are applied to net expected goals and incremental zone time, quantifying the market inefficiency of undervalued centers by projecting role-specific personnel usage onto probabilistic goal differentials.
gse_mapping: GSE treats each faceoff as a critical state-transition node in a Markovian game engine. The situational reasoning layer evaluates directional vectors and handedness to compute real-time offensive empowerment, dynamically updating the probability of game-changing offense based on the immediate post-faceoff puck possession topology.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Translating Faceoffs to Goals, Wins, and Championships in Hockey Other Sports 193940 Abstract Occurring around 60 times per game, hockey faceoffs uniquely start without any team possessing the puck but invariably end with one team in control.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N_f: Number of faceoffs per game (dimensionless count); P(t): Puck possession state (Boolean {0,1}); t_0: Time of drop (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes instantaneous resolution of the neutral possession state; ignores delayed whistles or procedural delays.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down during no-call penalties or dropped pucks where neither team achieves immediate control, creating a prolonged neutral state.

primitives.name: Net Expected Goals Differential Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper analyzes the importance and value of faceoffs in the context of the incremental puck possession and offense they afford.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: xG_net: Net expected goals (dimensionless probability mass); xG_off: Offensive expected goals generated (probability); xG_def: Defensive expected goals prevented (probability)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a linear superposition of expected goal values across multiple faceoff events within a single shift.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when defensive breakdowns occur so rapidly that the causal link between the faceoff win and the scoring chance is severed.

layer2.mapping: Directly feeds the GSI valuation matrix, converting mechanical wins into a scalar currency of goal expectancy for roster optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Expected Goal For % (xGF%) and Expected Goal Against % (xGA%) following faceoffs.

primitives.name: Incremental Zone Time Accumulator
primitives.verbatim_quote: This research fills the void by continuing the effort to translate faceoff results to scoring outcomes, measuring faceoff performance in goals, wins, and losses in a novel manner.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta T_{zone}: Incremental zone time gained (seconds); T_{win}: Duration of zone possession after win (seconds); T_{loss}: Duration before turnover after loss (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes zone time is a strictly monotonic function of sustained offensive pressure and scoring probability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities arise in 'dump and chase' scenarios where possession is lost immediately but deep icing prevents an immediate zone exit.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's temporal decay functions, extending the half-life of offensive zone opportunities based on the quality of the initial draw.
layer2.telemetry: Average Offensive Zone Time (OZT) per faceoff outcome.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by formalizing the faceoff not merely as a binary win/loss event, but as a high-frequency stochastic operator acting upon the spatial manifold of the ice rink. By isolating the 'incremental puck possession' (Quote 9), we establish a direct causal pathway from the micro-mechanics of the draw to macroscopic scoring outcomes. The core mathematical innovation lies in decoupling the raw correlation of faceoff win percentage from goal-scoring metrics, which previous literature dismissed as negligible. Instead, we construct a dual-metric system: Net Expected Goals (xG_net) and Incremental Zone Time (\Delta T_{zone}). These operators function as derived kernels that integrate the immediate aftermath of the draw—specifically directionality and handedness—into a cumulative probability mass. The duality exists between the offensive empowerment (generating xG) and defensive preservation (preventing xG against), treated as two sides of the same coin (Page 4). Failure modes emerge when the temporal window between the draw and the subsequent shot is too wide, causing the causal signal to drown in the noise of general play dynamics. Thus, the model imposes a strict temporal decay function, ensuring only immediate offensive events are attributed to the faceoff victory, preventing the over-valuation of coincidental scoring.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The lineage of this primitive traces back to early possession-based metrics in basketball and soccer, evolving through Schuckers et al.'s foundational work on weighted averages of faceoff directionality. However, it diverges sharply by rejecting the purely correlational approach of earlier articles [1]-[3] that deemed faceoffs statistically irrelevant. Instead, it adopts a mechanistic, objective-driven training paradigm, directly optimizing for expected goal creation rather than relying on post-hoc statistical coincidences.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling the opposing agents requires understanding the center's strategic intent during the draw. A victorious center is not just winning a coin toss; they are executing a decision tree aimed at specific spatial vulnerabilities (e.g., passing to a trailing winger vs. going strong). The General Manager acts as a meta-agent, utilizing these projections to maximize championship chances by exploiting market inefficiencies in player valuation, specifically undervaluing the tangible goal impact of elite faceoff talent.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict anti-collinearity veto is applied to prevent leakage between 'net expected goals' and general team shooting percentage. If a team's overall offensive rating is exceptionally high, the marginal contribution of a single faceoff must be dampened to avoid double-counting systemic strength. Furthermore, we veto any attribution of goals scored after the puck has cleared the offensive zone and re-entered, as the causal chain is effectively broken by the intervening neutral zone transition.
